GrappStar launcher, one motor, three one way bearings, piston pitch, motor fixed on the axle

TEST BUILD, snap together: every pin is printed with a head and a C clip groove, the axle is one printed piece with the D socket head, and three printed bushings stand in for the one way bearings (same size, swap later). The sim still shows the launcher working as it will with the bearings fitted. The big gear is now mounted on the rail itself (on a stub in the bracket) and the rail pivots on the motor axle, so the rack never slips when the pitch changes. A 12T drive gear with bearing A sits on the axle: forward turns drive the big gear (cock and fire), backward it freewheels. Bearing B in the 16T pinion: backward turns the 32T crank gear (module 8, 14 mm thick, same as the big gear), forward it freewheels. Bearing C in the pedestal is a backstop for the crank gear. The crank pin and the lug pin are 12 mm rods, same as the bearings, and the thick connecting rod (the piston) runs on them up to the lug on the rail: backward turns push the launcher up, 6° to 47°, and it stays there. With the big gear on the rail, both the launcher weight and the cocking pull push the piston the same way, so the backstop holds through the whole shot. Plain spur gears, 14 mm wide, solid; the last tooth on the big gear is cut down to the pitch line (tapered toward the rail) and the tooth before it is 30% taller, so the two let go within a degree of each other and the release load is shared. Rail beam 64 x 60, carriage widened to match. Spring posts and carriage pegs Ø44 and Ø32 with a wide bar behind each. Desk size (0.3). Drag to orbit, wheel to zoom, right-drag to pan.
